SMTO-SKL-0031 — Google Calendar reported a conflict with this event

GUID: fc831763-d1cd-523d-ab6f-072cbf9002b9
Slug: google-calendar-event-conflict
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • Google Calendar refused this change because it clashes with something already on the calendar. Often the event was already created by an earlier attempt, so a second copy wasn't made.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Google Calendar in your browser, signed in to the same Google account, and look for the event on its date in the calendar it was meant for. This conflict usually means the event already exists, so making it again would give you a duplicate.
  2. If the event is there, ask SMTO to show that event and make any remaining changes to it, rather than creating a new one. Changing the existing event keeps one meeting and one set of invitations for your guests.
  3. If the event is not there, ask SMTO to create it once more and approve the request. Once you have confirmed nothing was created, a single new attempt is safe.

What success looks like

  • Google Calendar shows exactly one copy of the event with the details you wanted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep asking SMTO to create the event again, and don't paste private calendar details into messages.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Calendar returned HTTP 409 (event_conflict) for the event or calendar write, typically because an event with the same SMTO-derived ID already exists.

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 409 for the Calendar operation. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 409 for the Calendar operation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact event identity and provider conflict detail.

How to fix it

  • Google returned 409 from the Calendar API (mapped in google_calendar/client.py provider_error). For create_event, the event ID is a hash of account, calendar and operation ID, so read that exact event ID with google_calendar.event before doing anything else; reconcile it instead of creating a replacement, and never generate another meeting automatically.
  • Read the exact event and resolve the reported conflict; do not create another meeting automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the exact event ID to reconcile an existing create. Do not generate another meeting automatically.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing event state is reconciled before any replacement create or edit.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
